title: Reading and Writing MATLAB Arrays with SciPy
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose of reading and writing matlab arrays with scipy.

understand.concept: SciPy's scipy.io module reads and writes MATLAB MAT files. loadmat returns a dictionary-like mapping containing stored variables, while savemat writes named variables. MATLAB and NumPy differ in conventions such as array orientation and metadata, so inspect variable names, shapes and dtypes after loading. For reproducible tests, in-memory file objects can avoid creating persistent files.

examples.title: Round-trip a vector in memory
examples.code:
from scipy.io import savemat, loadmat
from io import BytesIO
b=BytesIO()
savemat(b, {'scores':[1,2,3]})
b.seek(0)
data=loadmat(b)
print(data['scores'].ravel().tolist())
examples.explanation: This deterministic example demonstrates round-trip a vector in memory. Inspect the returned values and consider how the method's assumptions affect real datasets.

examples.title: Check a saved variable name
examples.code:
from scipy.io import savemat, loadmat
from io import BytesIO
b=BytesIO()
savemat(b, {'temperature':25})
b.seek(0)
print('temperature' in loadmat(b))
examples.explanation: This deterministic example demonstrates check a saved variable name. Inspect the returned values and consider how the method's assumptions affect real datasets.

examples.title: Inspect a matrix shape
examples.code:
from scipy.io import savemat, loadmat
from io import BytesIO
import numpy as np
b=BytesIO()
savemat(b, {'matrix':np.array([[1,2],[3,4]])})
b.seek(0)
print(loadmat(b)['matrix'].shape)
examples.explanation: This deterministic example demonstrates inspect a matrix shape. Inspect the returned values and consider how the method's assumptions affect real datasets.

examples.title: Write multiple variables
examples.code:
from scipy.io import savemat, loadmat
from io import BytesIO
b=BytesIO()
savemat(b, {'x':[1,2], 'y':[3,4]})
b.seek(0)
data=loadmat(b)
print(data['x'].ravel().tolist(), data['y'].ravel().tolist())
examples.explanation: This deterministic example demonstrates write multiple variables. Inspect the returned values and consider how the method's assumptions affect real datasets.

examples.title: Check loaded numeric dtype
examples.code:
from scipy.io import savemat, loadmat
from io import BytesIO
import numpy as np
b=BytesIO()
savemat(b, {'values':np.array([1.5,2.5])})
b.seek(0)
print(loadmat(b)['values'].dtype.kind)
examples.explanation: This deterministic example demonstrates check loaded numeric dtype. Inspect the returned values and consider how the method's assumptions affect real datasets.
